title: Pattern Expansion and Consolidation on Evolving Graphs for Continual Traffic Prediction

problem.claim: Traffic flow prediction must accommodate continuously expanding traffic networks.

gap.claim: Most existing traffic flow prediction models are designed for static traffic networks and do not model their continuous evolution and expansion.

contributions.claim: An efficient continual learning framework, PECPM, enables continuous traffic flow prediction on expanding networks without access to historical graph data.
A pattern bank based on pattern matching stores representative road-network patterns and is managed as the network expands.
Pattern expansion detects evolved and new patterns for addition to the bank, while pattern consolidation preserves learned patterns and maintains their traceability.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world traffic datasets are reported to show competitive performance.
Experiments on real-world traffic datasets are reported to show superior efficiency.
Experiments on real-world traffic datasets are reported to show strong generalization ability.

narrative_sequence.summary: Spatiotemporal graph convolutional networks have improved traffic flow prediction accuracy.
Existing models primarily target static traffic networks and fail to represent continuous network evolution and expansion.
The work addresses prediction on expanding networks with PECPM, using a pattern bank to support continual prediction without historical graph data.
Pattern expansion adds evolved or new patterns, while consolidation preserves learned patterns and their traceability.
Experiments on real-world traffic datasets report competitive performance, efficiency, and generalization.

source_observation.claim: A pattern bank is continuously updated with new patterns while learned patterns are consolidated as the traffic network expands.

interpretation.claim: Separating adaptation to new structure from preservation of prior knowledge can support continual learning under evolving graph structure.

application.claim: For other evolving graph prediction tasks, maintain a reusable representation store with explicit mechanisms for expansion and consolidation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy transfers beyond traffic prediction or across different types of graph evolution.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the model architecture or computational cost in detail.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported performance, efficiency, or generalization.
